extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the PARI/GP system (PARI/GEN library and GP calculator) seeking reference for functions and behaviors
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP numeric and symbolic library functions: concise descriptions of each function's semantics, edge cases, examples, and corresponding library (GEN) entry points. Intended to guide correct use and porting between GP and the GEN C API.

rubrics_metrics.name: divrem(x, y) / remainder of division
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns quotient and remainder of division of x by y; remainder is x - (x\y)*y. Useful to avoid two divisions when both quotient and remainder are needed. If v is present and x,y are multivariate polynomials, divide with respect to variable v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveat: divrem(x,y)[2] is not generally the same as x % y; no GP operator corresponds to it. Examples show behavior with rationals and modular objects and that forbidden divisions may raise errors (e.g. divrem(Mod(2,9),3)[2] raises forbidden division t_INTMOD \ t_INT). Library syntax: GEN divrem(GEN x, GEN y, long v = -1). Also available: GEN gdiventres(GEN x, GEN y) when v is not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: lex(x, y) — lexicographic comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns −1, 0 or 1 for lexicographic comparison of x and y. Comparison is admissible across different types (scalars, vectors, matrices) as long as scalars are comparable, and is recursive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If components equal up to smallest length, the more complex (longer) operand is larger. For equal lengths: matrix > vector > scalar. Examples: lex([1,3],[1,2,5]) = 1; lex([1,3],[1,3,-1]) = −1; lex([1],[[1]]) = −1; lex([1],[1]~) = 0. Library: GEN lexcmp(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: max(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates the maximum of x and y when they can be compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only valid when x and y are comparable under GP's comparison rules. Library: GEN gmax(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: min(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates the minimum of x and y when they can be compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only valid when x and y are comparable under GP's comparison rules. Library: GEN gmin(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: powers(x, n, {x0})
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-negative n, returns vector with n+1 components [1, x, ..., x^n] if x0 omitted; if x0 given returns [x0, x0*x, ..., x0*x^n]. When n < 0 returns empty vector [].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include modular and matrix powers and starting value x0 usage. Library syntax: GEN gpowers0(GEN x, long n, GEN x0 = NULL); GEN gpowers(GEN x, long n) when x0 is NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: shift(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise shift of x: left shift by n (n≥0) multiplies by 2^n; right shift by |n| (n<0) shifts componentwise right by |n| bits which corresponds to Euclidean division by 2^{|n|} with remainder of same sign as x (not identical to ordinary division by 2^{|n|}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations: x << n or x >> (−n). Note right shift differs from x\2^n for signed integers because Euclidean division semantics used. Library: GEN gshift(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: shiftmul(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplies x by 2^n. Difference with shift: when n<0 ordinary division is performed and result may be fractional; shift with n<0 uses Euclidean division so integers remain integers when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you want arithmetic multiply/divide by powers of 2 (with ordinary division semantics for negative n). Library: GEN gmul2n(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: sign(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign of x (0, 1 or −1). x must be integer, real or fraction; t_QUAD with positive discriminants and t_INFINITY supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN gsigne(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecmax(x, {&v})
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is a vector or matrix returns the largest entry of x; otherwise returns a copy of x. Error if x is empty. If v provided, set it to index (vector) or coordinates [i,j] (matrix) of a largest entry; ignored for non-vector/matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: vecmax([10,20,-30,40]) = 40; vecmax([10,20,-30,40], &v) sets v=4; vecmax on matrix returns value and coordinates. Library: GEN vecmax0(GEN x, GEN *v = NULL); GEN vecmax(GEN x) when v not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: vecmin(x, {&v})
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is a vector or matrix returns the smallest entry of x; otherwise returns a copy of x. Error if x is empty. If v provided, set it to index or coordinates of a smallest entry; ignored for non-vector/matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples analogous to vecmax. Library: GEN vecmin0(GEN x, GEN *v = NULL); GEN vecmin(GEN x) when v not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison and Boolean operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Six standard comparisons <=, <, >=, >, ==, != return 1 for true and 0 for false. == is liberal (e.g., integer 0, 0 polynomial, and vector with 0 entries test equal). === tests strict identity (objects of different type or length never identical). Strings (t_STR) compared lexicographically; comparing strings to different types raises exception. Boolean operators ||, &&, ! available. <> is synonym for !=. '=' is assignment (not equality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of liberal semantics of == versus strict identity ===; mixing types (especially strings) can raise exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Col(x, {n}) — column conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms x into a column vector. If n omitted or 0, dimension depends on x's type (usually single component except special cases). If n provided, zeros are appended if n>0 or prepended if n<0; resulting vector dimension is |n|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases: if x is a vector or quadratic form, result is initial object as row vector; polynomial -> vector of coefficients starting with leading coefficient; power series -> significant coefficients by increasing degree (Vec reciprocal to Pol/Ser). For matrix or string, n must be omitted or error. Library: GEN gtocol0(GEN x, long n); GEN gtocol(GEN x). See Vec for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colrev(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalent to Col(x, −n) then reverse the result. Reciprocal of Polrev: coefficients start with constant coefficient then increasing degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN gtocolrev0(GEN x, long n); GEN gtocolrev(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: List({x = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms a (row or column) vector x into a list with components entries of x; for other types creates a 1-element list. Creating a non-empty list (except when x omitted) creates a small memory leak; initialize lists to empty or use sparingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mklist(void) for empty list. Library: GEN gtolist(GEN x = NULL); GEN mklist(void).

rubrics_metrics.name: Map({x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates an associative array (dictionary) from matrix [a1,b1; ...; an,bn] mapping ai→bi. If x omitted creates empty map that can be filled via mapput.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: M = Map(factor(13!)); mapget(M,3) = 5. Library: GEN gtomap(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mat({x = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms x into a matrix. If x already a matrix, returns copy. Row/column vector -> 1-row/1-column matrix unless elements are column/row vectors of same length, in which case concatenation yields a bigger matrix. Binary quadratic form -> attached 2×2 matrix. Otherwise 1×1 matrix containing x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given of Mat on vectors and Qfb. Library: GEN gtomat(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mod(a, b) — modular objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates an intmod or a polmod (a mod b). b must be integer or polynomial. Produces t_INTMOD for integers or t_POLMOD for polynomials. If a%b yields appropriate type, Mod(a,b) succeeds as well. Modular objects have internal modulus knowledge (unlike x % y) and can be lifted via lift/centerlift; modulus recovered via z.mod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show differences between x = 4 % 5 and x = Mod(4,5) when adding 1. For complex objects base change to Z/bZ or K[x]/(b) happens (faster than multiplying by Mod(1,b)). Library: GEN gmodulo(GEN a, GEN b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pol(t, {v = x}) — to polynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms t into a polynomial with main variable v. If t scalar -> constant polynomial. If t is power series with non-negative valuation or rational function -> similar to truncate (chop O(X^k) or compute Euclidean quotient). Main use: when t is a vector it creates polynomial with coefficients from t[1] being leading coefficient. Much faster evaluating Pol on coefficient vector than naive expression expansion. Warning: not a substitution function — variable priority rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Pol([1,2,3]) = x^2 + 2*x +3. Pol(x+y, y) raises "variable must have higher priority" error. Library: GEN gtopoly(GEN t, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polrev(t, {v = x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms t into polynomial with main variable v where t[1] is constant term (reverse ordering). For power series it behaves like truncate. Reciprocal function is Vecrev.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Polrev([1,2,3]) = 3*x^2 + 2*x + 1. Library: GEN gtopolyrev(GEN t, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qfb(a, b, c, {D = 0.}) — binary quadratic form
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates binary quadratic form a x^2 + b x y + c y^2. If b^2 − 4ac > 0 initialize Shanks' distance function to D. Negative definite forms are not implemented — use positive definite counterpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN Qfb0(GEN a, GEN b, GEN c, GEN D = NULL, long prec) or qfi (assumes b^2 − 4ac <0) and qfr (assumes b^2 − 4ac >0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ser(s, {v = x}, {d = seriesprecision}) — to power series
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms s into a power series with main variable v and precision (number of significant terms) d ≥ 0. If s scalar -> constant series with precision d. If s polynomial, truncated to d terms if needed. If d omitted, uses exact amount of information in input: returns series verbatim if s already series; if s vector, vector entries interpreted as coefficients starting from constant term; if d explicitly given, truncates or extends with zeros to d significant terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show default seriesprecision and explicit d behavior. Warning: not a substitution function — variable priority rules apply. Library: GEN Ser0(GEN s, long v = -1, GEN d = NULL, long precdl).

rubrics_metrics.name: Set({x = []}) — make a set
rubrics_metrics.description: Converts x into a set (row vector) with strictly increasing entries according to universal comparison function cmp. Standard container types converted to sets of corresponding elements; other types -> set with single element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Set([1,2,4,2,1,3]) = [1,2,3,4]. Library: GEN gtoset(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Str({x}*) — concatenate as string
rubrics_metrics.description: Concatenates its argument list into a single character string (t_STR); empty string if omitted. Arguments evaluated in string context. To recover GEN from string apply eval to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mostly useless in library mode; use strtoGEN/GENtostr to convert between GEN and char*. GENtostr returns malloced string that should be freed. Example: Str(x, i) with x2=0,i=2 yields "x2" and eval yields 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strchr(x) — integer-to-character string
rubrics_metrics.description: Converts x to a string by translating each integer into a character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Strchr(97) = "a"; Vecsmall("hello world") yields vector of ASCII codes; Strchr(Vecsmall(...)) returns the string. Library: GEN Strchr(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strexpand({x}*) — environment expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Concatenates arguments into a string and performs environment expansion (e.g. $HOME). Arguments read in string context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Strexpand("$HOME/doc") yields "/home/pari/doc". Useful to read environment variable values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strtex({x}*) — TeX translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Translates arguments to TeX format and concatenates into single string. Arguments read in string context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to obtain TeX representation of expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vec(x, {n}) — to row vector
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms x into a row vector. If n omitted or 0 dimension depends on type. Special cases: vector or quadratic form -> initial object as row vector; polynomial -> vector of coefficients starting with leading coefficient; power series -> significant coefficients by increasing order (valuation ignored); matrix -> vector of columns; string -> vector of characters; map -> domain vector; error context -> error components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If n provided and not meaningless, zeros are appended if n>0 or prepended if n<0, dimension |n|. Vec is reciprocal of Pol for polynomials and Ser for power series of valuation 0. Examples and helper serVec function illustrate usage. Library: GEN gtovec0(GEN x, long n); GEN gtovec(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vecrev(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalent to Vec(x, −n) then reverse the result. Reciprocal of Polrev: coefficients start with constant term then increasing degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN gtovecrev0(GEN x, long n); GEN gtovecrev(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vecsmall(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms x into a row vector of type t_VECSMALL; acts like Vec but only for objects representable as a vector of small integers. If x is a string returns vector of ASCII codes. n has same zero-append/prepend semantics when meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN gtovecsmall0(GEN x, long n); GEN gtovecsmall(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: binary(x) — binary digit expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs vector of binary digits of |x|. For integer x returns binary digits; for real returns two components (integer part and fractional part expansions). For vector/matrix returns per-component structure. 0 has no digits (empty vector []).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show binary(10) = [1,0,1,0]; binary(3.14) returns nested representations. Library: GEN binaire(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: bitand(x, y) — bitwise and
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise and of two integers computed as sum (xi and yi)2^i. Negative numbers behave 2-adically (result is 2-adic limit); result is ordinary integer possibly negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: bitand(5,3)=1; bitand(-5,3)=3; bitand(-5,-3)=-7. Library: GEN gbitand(GEN x, GEN y). Also GEN ibitand(GEN x, GEN y) returns bitwise and of |x| and |y| for two integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitneg(x, {n = −1}) — bitwise negation
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise negation of integer x truncated to n bits (n≥0) computed as sum not(xi)2^i for i=0..n−1. Special case n=−1 means no truncation and infinite sequence of leading 1 represented as negative number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior for negative arguments follows 2-adic conventions in Section 3.6.20. Library: GEN gbitneg(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: bitnegimply(x, y) — bitwise negated imply
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise negated implication (not (x ⇒ y)) computed bitwise as (xi andnot(yi))2^i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See negative argument behavior in bitand. Library: GEN gbitnegimply(GEN x, GEN y); GEN ibitnegimply(GEN x, GEN y) for absolute values.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitor(x, y) — bitwise inclusive or
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise inclusive OR of two integers (xi or yi)2^i. Negative numbers follow 2-adic conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN gbitor(GEN x, GEN y); GEN ibitor(GEN x, GEN y) for absolute values.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitprecision(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: If n omitted returns floating-point precision in bits of PARI object x; returns +oo for exact objects. If n present and positive creates new object equal to x with new bit-precision roughly n (rounded up to nearest multiple of 64 or 32). For vectors/matrices operation done componentwise; for series/polynomials done coefficientwise. For real x, n is number of desired significant bits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show bitprecision(exp(1e-100)) = 512 bits; bitprecision(1,10) = 1. Library: GEN bitprecision0(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: bittest(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs the nth bit of x (starting from right, coefficient of 2^n) returning 0 or 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior for negative x behaves 2-adically; examples: bittest(7,0)=1, bittest(7,3)=0. Library: GEN gbittest(GEN x, long n). Low-level variants available for t_INT inputs: long bittest(GEN x, long n) and ulong int_bit(GEN x, long n) for n≥0.

rubrics_metrics.name: bitxor(x, y) — bitwise exclusive or
rubrics_metrics.description: Bitwise XOR of two integers computed as (xi xor yi)2^i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative argument behavior per bitand. Library: GEN gbitxor(GEN x, GEN y); GEN ibitxor(GEN x, GEN y) for absolute values.

rubrics_metrics.name: ceil(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ceiling of x. For real x returns smallest integer ≥ x. For rational functions returns Euclidean quotient of numerator by denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN gceil(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: centerlift(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Like lift, but t_INTMOD and t_PADIC components lifted using centered residues: for t_INTMOD x∈Z/nZ the lift y satisfies −n/2 < y ≤ n/2. For t_PADIC with non-negative valuation use centered lift modulo ppadicprec(x); if valuation negative returns fraction p^v centerlift(x p^{−v}); rational reconstruction not attempted. Alias lift(x,'v) allowed for backward compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when centered representatives are desired rather than standard canonical lifts. Library: centerlift(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: characteristic(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the characteristic of the base ring over which x is defined (as defined by t_INTMOD and t_FFELT components). Raises exception if incompatible primes arise between components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: characteristic(Mod(1,24)*x + Mod(1,18)*y) = 6. Library: GEN characteristic(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: component(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extracts the nth component of x as defined by GEN internal layout: components counted after initial type code words. For vector -> nth component; matrix -> nth column; polynomial -> nth coefficient (degree n−1); series -> nth significant coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer polcoeff for polynomials and [ ] operator for vectors/matrices. Using component requires detailed knowledge of PARI types and should almost never be used directly. Examples show extracting p-adic accuracy words. Library: GEN compo(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: conj(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate of x. For real quadratic numbers conjugation is in that real quadratic field. No effect on integers, reals, intmods, fractions or p-adics. t_POLMOD is forbidden (use conjvec).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN gconj(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: conjvec(z) — conjugate vector representation
rubrics_metrics.description: For polmod z = Mod(a,T) returns vector of length degree(T) containing complex embeddings of z if T has rational coefficients (a(r[i]) where r = polroots(T)), or conjugates if T has intmod coefficients. For finite field elements returns [z, z^p, z^{p^2}, ...]. If z integer or rational returns z. If z row/column vector returns matrix whose columns are conjugate vectors of components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN conjvec(GEN z, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: denominator(f, {D})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns denominator of f. For integer or polynomial treated as rational number/function denominator equals 1. For recursive structures (vectors/matrices) returns lcm of denominators of components (common denominator). For t_INTMOD and t_PADIC denominator is 1; denominator of t_POLMOD is denominator of its lift. Optional argument D controls ring over which denominator computed: D=1 uses Q-structure (returns positive integer); D='x treats entries as rational functions in K(x) and returns polynomial in x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate different D choices: denominator(x + 1/y + 1/2) as t_POL in x yields 1; denominator(...,1) yields 2; denominator(..., y) yields 2*y. Library: GEN denominator(GEN f, GEN D = NULL). Convenience variants: GEN denom(GEN x), GEN Q_denom(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: digits(x, {b = 10})
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs vector of digits of |x| in base b (b=10 default). 0 has no digits (empty vector []).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: digits(123) = [1,2,3]; digits(10,2) = [1,0,1,0]. Library: GEN digits(GEN x, GEN b = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: exponent(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: For t_REAL returns binary exponent e such that 2^e ≤ |x| < 2^{e+1}. For non-zero integers exponent defined naturally; exponent of exact 0 is −oo. For t_FRAC a/b exponent is exponent(a) − exponent(b). For compound types (t_COMPLEX, t_POL, t_SER, t_VEC, t_COL, t_MAT) returns max exponent among components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for bounds: 2^{e+1} is quick sup-norm bound for reals; examples given. Library: GEN gpexponent(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: floor(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Floor of x. For real x returns largest integer ≤ x. For rational function returns Euclidean quotient of numerator by denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN gfloor(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: frac(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fractional part of x, identical to x − floor(x). For real x result in [0,1[.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN gfrac(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: fromdigits(x, {b = 10})
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives integer formed by elements of x viewed as digits in base b (reverse of digits). By convention, fromdigits([])=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: fromdigits([1,4,4,1,4],5) = 1234. Library: GEN fromdigits(GEN x, GEN b = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: imag(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imaginary part of x. For quadratic numbers this is the coefficient of ω in canonical integral basis (1, ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN gimag(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: length(x) / #x
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of x: for vectors dimension (0 for empty), lists number of entries, matrices number of columns, strings number of characters (excluding trailing \0). For arbitrary GP types returns number of non-code words in x (awkward for most types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: #"a string" = 8; #[] = 0; #matrix(2,5) = 5. Library: long glength(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: lift(x, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Lifts components: intmods from Z/nZ to Z, p-adics from Qp to Q (as truncate), polmods to polynomials when v omitted. If v given only polmods whose modulus has main variable v are lifted. t_FFELT not lifted; List elements not lifted (convert to vectors or use apply(lift,L)). Components for which lift is meaningless copied verbatim. Lifts performed recursively but only one level (once polmod lifted its components not lifted further).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate tricky interactions when mixing moduli and variables. Alternatives: liftall (fully recursive), liftint, liftpol, centerlift. Library: GEN lift0(GEN x, long v = -1) and GEN lift(GEN x) for default.

rubrics_metrics.name: liftall(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursively lift all components of x from Z/nZ to Z, Qp to Q, and polmods to polynomials, as long as possible. t_FFELT not lifted; List elements not lifted (use apply(liftall,L) or convert to vectors). Components for which lifts meaningless copied verbatim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show lifting nested modular components. Library: GEN liftall(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: liftint(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursively lift all components of x from Z/nZ to Z and from Qp to Q (truncate). t_FFELT not lifted; Lists not lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when only integer and p-adic lifts desired. Library: GEN liftint(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: liftpol(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursively lift all components of x which are polmods to polynomials. t_FFELT and List elements not lifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when only polynomial lifts wanted. Library: GEN liftpol(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: norm(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algebraic norm of x: product of x with its conjugate (or conjugates for polmods). For vectors and matrices norm is taken componentwise (not L2 norm). The norm of an element of R is its square to stay compatible with complex norm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library: GEN gnorm(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: numerator(f, {D})
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator of f defined as f * denominator(f,D). Optional D controls ring (same semantics as denominator): D=1 for Q-denominator, D='x for polynomial-in-x denominator, or NULL default behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: numerator(x + 1/y + 1/2, 1) and other D choices illustrate results. Convenience wrappers: GEN numer(GEN x) and GEN Q_remove_denom(GEN x, GEN *ptd) which also returns the denominator. Library: GEN numerator(GEN f, GEN D = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: oo (infinity object)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns object representing +∞ (oo). Can be negated (-oo for −∞) and compared to real numbers with usual ordering: +∞ greater than any real, −∞ smaller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use in functions such as intnum where infinities are meaningful. Library: GEN mkoo().

rubrics_metrics.name: padicprec(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns absolute p-adic precision of x: minimum precision of components of x; returns +oo if x is exact (as p-adic). Raises exception if encountering object incompatible with p-adic computations (wrong modulus or type).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show padicprec((1 + O(2^5))*x + (2 + O(2^4)),2) = 4 and that padicprec can raise errors for inconsistent moduli or incorrect types. Library: GEN gppadicprec(GEN x, GEN p); long padicprec(GEN x, GEN p) returns LONG_MAX if x=0 and p-adic precision as long.

rubrics_metrics.name: precision(x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: If n omitted returns floating point precision in decimal digits of x; returns +oo if x has no floating-point component. If n present creates a new object equal to x with floating point precision n (number of significant decimal digits). For non-floating types no change. For compounds returns minimal accuracy among components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: precision(exp(1e-100)) = 154 decimal digits; precision(2 + x) = +oo. Library: GEN precision0(GEN x, long n); GEN gprec(GEN x, long n); long precision(GEN x) (accuracy expressed in words on platform).

rubrics_metrics.name: random({N = 2^31})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a random element depending on argument N and its type: if N is integer returns uniform integer in [0, N−1] (default random(2^31)). If N is real returns real in [0,1[ with accuracy like N. If N is t_INTMOD returns random intmod for same modulus. If t_FFELT returns random element of finite field. If N is t_VEC of length 2 returns integer uniformly in [a,b]. If N is t_VEC from ellinit over finite field returns a random affine k-rational point (not uniform over E(k)). If N is t_POL returns random polynomial of degree ≤ degree(N) with coefficients drawn by applying random to leading coefficient of N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware distribution choices: e.g., elliptic-curve point drawing is not uniformly distributed over E(k) but usually sufficient for applications. Library: GEN random(GEN N = NULL).
